cache: Here the website keeps a copy of a recent ticket count so it can answer a later request quickly.
trade-off: a gain with an accompanying cost
Reusing a count saves time, but the answer may be out of date.
stale: A saved count becomes stale as soon as a booking changes the real count, even if the saved entry can still be used.
time to live: The website is allowed to reuse a saved answer for thirty seconds after storing it.
cache hit: The website finds a count it can still use and avoids asking the booking system again.
expires: reaches the end of its allowed lifetime
After thirty seconds, another visit makes the website request a fresh count.
discrepancy: difference between values that should agree
A cached count of twelve disagrees with the booking system’s current count of eight.
tolerate: The exhibition list remains useful even if a recent change takes a few minutes to appear.
cache invalidation: discarding a stored answer that can no longer be trusted
A booking update triggers removal of the saved count for that tour.
cache miss: no reusable stored answer was found
When there is no usable count for the requested tour, the website asks the booking system for one.
expiry: end of the allowed reuse period
A fixed expiry keeps a lost notice from leaving the same count in use indefinitely.
cache key: identifier used to find a stored answer
The date and tour together identify which saved ticket count to use.
